label: Assistant
text:
The frozen benchmark is complete in `/workspace/submission` (run.py, evaluation.json, README.md, item assets, vendored SDK). It declares 110 distinct questions, each independently scored, with three frozen weighted-mean domain aggregations.

**What the suite measures**
- Reasoning (30 items): HLE text-only questions, upstream system prompt, local letter/normalized matching with a cheap helper-simulator equivalence judge as fallback.
- Coding (38 items): 20 SciCode dev-split sub-steps executed against targets computed from the gold solutions, plus 18 LiveCodeBench v6 problems (12 hard, 6 medium) run in subprocesses; binary all-tests-pass scoring.
- Co-work (42 items): 26 authored multi-constraint instruction-following prompts with deterministic checkers (system-prompt rules, multi-turn histories, format and count constraints), plus 16 text-only GDPval tasks graded by helper-grader against filtered upstream rubrics (weight 1.5).

**Key findings that shaped the protocol**
- No container runtime exists here, so repository-level SWE tasks were impossible; coding is measured by scientific and algorithmic programming instead.
- Max-effort candidates think far past modest output caps. ArXivMath was dropped after every tested model exhausted 32k tokens without answering. Development-01 costs about $30 per million output tokens, so caps had to fit a $30 suite budget: HLE 14k, SciCode 14k, LCB 16k, IF 5k, GDPval 16k, with each prompt stating its limit.
- Feedback on a 14-item snapshot across three models gave Pearson 0.96 for GDPval, 0.56 for DeepSWE, and −0.95 for SWE-bench Multilingual, the latter because development-08 truncated under the old caps while being the strongest reference model there.
- The full 110-item suite completed on development-01 in 56 minutes for $17.08 with 110/110 items scored. Domain scores were coding 0.87, co-work 0.70, reasoning 0.30. Nine of 16 GDPval deliverables truncated at the 8k cap then in force, so the frozen version raises that cap to 16k; this last change was not re-measured.

**Limitations kept visible in the README**
- Cheap long-thinking candidates lose items to truncation; some providers bill hidden reasoning beyond the cap, so the cost bound is approximate.
- Only one full-suite measurement completed; per-target correlation feedback covered three targets on a small snapshot. Rules were chosen from probes and cost constraints, not fitted to labels.
- Development spend was about $21 of the $100 wallet. A full run of the older revision on development-08 was still executing at the end of the window and can be inspected later via the job id in `/workspace/full1_jobs.json`.
